quote: op.execute("CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY refunds_order_idx ON refunds (order_id)")
title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY runs inside Alembic's migration transaction, which PostgreSQL rejects (the downgrade has the same fault)
evidence: upgrade() calls op.execute directly (line 12) and downgrade() does the same for DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY (line 18). Neither is wrapped in `with op.get_context().autocommit_block():`. Alembic runs PostgreSQL migrations with transactional DDL by default. No env.py or alembic.ini in the workspace sets autocommit or `transaction_per_migration`. I could not run Alembic or PostgreSQL here, so this is traced from Alembic's documented behaviour, not executed.
failing_case: `alembic upgrade head` on PostgreSQL reaches 3b1f and fails with `ActiveSqlTransaction: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block`. The release stops at this step. `alembic downgrade 2a0e` fails the same way at line 18, after the column drop on line 17 has been rolled back with the failed transaction, so the rollback path is broken too.
remediation: Wrap both CONCURRENTLY statements in `with op.get_context().autocommit_block():` and keep the ADD COLUMN outside it. Run a CI job that upgrades and downgrades against a real PostgreSQL.

title: 0007 depends on a migration named 0006_product_slug that does not exist; the file in the tree is 0006_safe
evidence: shop/migrations holds only 0006_safe.py and 0007_backfill.py (glob of the whole workspace). Django names a migration after its file, so the node is (shop, 0006_safe). Grep for 0006_product_slug finds only this line. 0006_safe.py line 9 also depends on (shop, 0005_initial), which is not in the tree either.
failing_case: Run `python manage.py migrate` (or `makemigrations`, `showmigrations`) on a checkout of this commit. Django builds the graph and raises NodeNotFoundError: Migration shop.0007_backfill dependencies reference nonexistent parent node ('shop', '0006_product_slug'). No migration in the app runs, so the deploy stops. If 0006_product_slug is the intended parent, the 0006_safe file is orphaned and the slug/NULL cleanup in it never precedes the 0007 backfill.
remediation: Make the dependency match the real parent name (`("shop", "0006_safe")`) or rename the 0006 file to 0006_product_slug. Add a CI step that runs `migrate --plan` or `makemigrations --check` against an empty database.

title: Backfill saves every column of each product row, so it can overwrite concurrent updates, and runs row by row in one transaction
evidence: fill_slugs lines 6-8 loads every Product with slug="" through the historical model, then calls p.save() with no update_fields. Django's save() writes all fields from the in-memory copy. Django migrations on PostgreSQL are atomic by default, so the loop is one long transaction and it takes row locks as it goes.
failing_case: The app keeps serving during the deploy (the point of an expand/backfill step). Product 42 has slug="". The migration loads it, then an admin changes its price or stock. The migration reaches p.save() and writes the old price and stock back with the slug. The admin's edit is lost with no error. On a large catalogue, N separate UPDATEs make this window long and hold row locks until the final commit, so concurrent writers to those rows block.
remediation: Do the backfill in SQL or as a queryset update that touches only slug, for example `Product.objects.filter(slug="").update(slug=Cast("pk", CharField()))`, in batches. For a large table, set `atomic = False` on the migration so each batch commits.

quote: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN tracking_code text;
title: Both SQL migrations have no down step and are not marked one-way
evidence: db/migrations/0001_safe.sql and 0002_orders.sql contain only forward statements (add column, index, constraints). No down section, no paired down file, and no comment saying the migration is one-way. The alembic and Django migrations in the same change do ship reverse steps.
failing_case: 0002 is deployed and the FK validation or the new index causes trouble in production. To roll back, an operator has to hand-write DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_fk, DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_idx and DROP COLUMN tracking_code under pressure. If 0002 failed part-way, nothing in the repo says which statements already committed, since CONCURRENTLY statements cannot sit in a rollback-able transaction.
remediation: Add a down section or paired down file for each SQL migration (drop constraint, drop index concurrently, drop column in reverse order), or mark the file one-way with a comment that says why.
